scoring.description: Each score is the percentile rank (0-100, ties at mid-rank) of a reading within that indicator's own history up to and including the observation date. Ranks do not depend on how a metric is expressed, so NUPL and MVRV, which are rescalings of each other, score identically. Because every historical score only uses data available on its date, the timeline does not use hindsight; the latest score is ranked against the full history. No score is published until an indicator has two years of history.

rounding.description: Every published number is rounded once, on its exact value, with ties going away from zero: scores and changes to 1 decimal, latest values to 6 decimals, history values to 4 significant digits.

composite.label: Cycle Index
composite.membership_rule: One representative per underlying quantity; no structurally trending series; only directional, cycle-scale measures. Members stay correlated (most are valuation ratios), so the index is a breadth summary rather than a set of independent votes.

excluded.note: NUPL equals 1 - 1/MVRV, a rescaling of MVRV.
The ratio has drifted upward across Bitcoin's history, so its percentile leans high regardless of cycle position.
Short-term NUPL is a rescaling of short-term MVRV.
Long-term NUPL is a rescaling of long-term MVRV.
Price divided by short-term realized price is short-term MVRV.
Price divided by realized price is MVRV.
Price divided by long-term realized price is long-term MVRV.
Price divided by the 200-day average is the Mayer Multiple.
Volatility spikes at both blow-off tops and capitulation lows, so a high reading does not indicate cycle position.
A 20-day band position swings across its whole range within weeks and would add noise to a cycle-scale index.
Fee rates have fallen structurally, pinning the percentile near 0 for most of the last five years.
Revenue per unit of hashrate declines almost monotonically as hashrate grows, pinning the percentile near 0.
